topic: Regression on table values of g(x) = f(x)/(x - 3)
problem:
The function g is defined by g(x) = f(x)/(x - 3), where f is a quadratic function. The table shows three values of x and their corresponding values of g(x).
x | g(x)
1 | 5
2 | 3
4 | 23
What is the value of f(3)?

bad.why: Writing f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, turning each table row into an equation such as (a + b + c)/(-2) = 5, and solving the 3-by-3 system by hand is long algebra.
g(3) is undefined (the denominator is zero), so evaluating g at x = 3 cannot answer; the question asks for f(3), which needs f's coefficients first.

algebraFirst.description: Multiplies each g-value by x - 3 to get f(1) = -10, f(2) = -3, f(4) = 23, sets up three equations in a, b, c, solves to f(x) = 2x^2 + x - 13, and evaluates f(3) = 8.

explanationNotes: g is undefined at x = 3 because its denominator is zero, but f is an ordinary quadratic, so f(3) exists. Regress the table against f(x)/(x - 3) so Desmos finds f's coefficients (a = 2, b = 1, c = -13) without converting the table by hand, then evaluate f(3) = 8. Make clear the table lists g-values, not f-values.
